A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentCoMa and contain complete, readable 28-page papers with Appendices A–N. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of the scientific content, figures and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 61 LLMs, a 45-participant human study, and interpretability experiments, with outcomes in Tables 2–5 and Figures 7–9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original LLM evaluations, human-study results and interpretability experiments, together with supplementary empirical results through Appendix N.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, CoT and self-ask procedures, and Min-K%++, attention and neuron-attribution analyses remain unchanged (Sections 3–6; Appendices C–E). No method component or inference procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same five AgentCoMa domains, Bamboogle and MultiArith. The additional-context scenario and reversed-order reasoning tasks in Appendix N are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the 61-model evaluation, representative 16-model comparisons, API-model results, human comparison and self-ask experiment (Tables 2, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 11).

E3.justification: Both retain the 80/180 development/test split, two-shot prompting, greedy decoding, accuracy evaluation and generation limits. The human-study design and Appendix N's 30-sample reversed-order protocol are identical.

E4.justification: The self-ask, additional-context, membership-inference, attention, neuron-overlap, judge-validation, failure-mode and reversed-order analyses retain the same questions and evidence (Section 6; Appendices C, G and K–N).

E5.justification: The single-run reporting in Figure 3 and Table 11, error bars in Figure 7, variance and standard deviation in Table 3, and pairwise t-tests in Appendix M are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative outcomes match throughout the main text and appendices. The abstract replaces '∼30%' with 'nearly 30%', restating the unchanged 29% average compositionality gap reported in Section 5.

T1.justification: The compositionality-gap definition, metric explanations and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, LLM compositionality-gap claims, human comparison and explanatory claims. The approximate-percentage rewording does not materially change their meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning training-data familiarity, contextual hallucination and neuron activation remain unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning controlled tasks and the small reversed-order study (Section 6; Limitations; Appendix N).

D1.justification: Model identifiers, hyperparameters, prompts, the four A100 GPUs and vLLM setup, and annotation instructions are unchanged. The project's code, data and leaderboard access information is also identical.

R1.justification: The Plaat et al. survey reference changes from a 2025 preprint to a 2026 journal entry, with corresponding citation-year and link updates. This is bibliographic updating of the same work; the cited-work set and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract changes '∼30%' to 'nearly 30%', affiliation markers change, and the Plaat et al. citation metadata are updated. These are limited editorial changes; section order and appendix organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The abstract and updated reference entry have minor text reflow, accompanied by small author-header typesetting changes. All ten figures and fifteen tables retain their displays, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: The updated survey citation, equivalent percentage wording and minor typesetting changes do not materially affect clarity or scientific reliability. Methods, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations—including all appendices—remain unchanged, supporting no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
